_meta.adr: ADR-037 modular manifest fragment — never edit src/manifest.json
_meta.description: Slice 10 of the bookkeeping-purchase-order-3way chain adds the Vendor Performance index + detail surfaces — the visible artefact of the monthly aggregation cron. Both pages render the basis-point rates (on-time delivery, quantity accuracy, price accuracy, invoice accuracy), the weighted overall score, the trend pill (improving / stable / declining) and the auto-review eligibility badge. The detail view also links back to the supplier's POs and SupplierInvoices for drill-through. Registered as kind=page custom components in src/registry.js because the standard generated index does not render basis-point rates as percentage pills or a colour-coded trend indicator, and the detail view adds the bespoke score breakdown.

pages.title: Vendor performance
pages._note: VendorPerformance stores one scorecard per (supplierId, period); this page shows ONE ROW PER SUPPLIER — the latest period only. That per-group latest-row reduction happens after the fetch and has no declarative equivalent: `type: index` renders the rows the query returns, so it would list every historical period per supplier. Decompose this page once the shared index gains a latest-per-group source; the rest of it (columns, eligibility facet, drill-through) is already ordinary index behaviour.

pages.title: Vendor performance
pages._note: The four component rates (onTimeDelivery, quantityAccuracy, priceAccuracy, invoiceAccuracy) are stored in BASIS POINTS and must render as percentage pills, and the period-over-period trend is computed against the previous period's scorecard — a second object the page fetches itself. `type: detail` renders the fields of the one object it resolved, with no basis-point formatter and no access to the previous period. Decompose this page once a basis-point/percentage formatter and a previous-period comparison exist in the shared library; the 'Related' drill-through to the supplier's purchase orders, supplier invoices and three-way matches is already expressible as config.relatedCollections.
